text:
**Bottom Line**

Score: **6.5/10**. I would **not approve this as-is**. The code is small, readable, and has a decent test suite, but the SQLite upsert logic has real data correctness bugs that can silently corrupt accounting results.

Tests: `61 passed`. `compileall` could not write `__pycache__` because `/work` is read-only for bytecode output.

**Issues**

| Severity | File | Lines | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| high | [db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70) | 70-84 | Older same-rank lifecycle records can overwrite fresher terminal records because updates do not compare reference timestamps. |
| high | [db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:74) | 74-80 | Re-ingest treats rows as unchanged when only state/end/elapsed match, ignoring changed user, partition, CPU, GPU, submit/start, and exit code fields. |
| medium | [db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:31) | 31-41,70-73 | Unknown Slurm states default to terminal rank, so active states like `CONFIGURING` can block later valid `RUNNING` updates. |
| medium | [parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:110) | 110-114,148-162 | Negative GPU or CPU counts are accepted and can produce negative usage-hour reports. |
| medium | [reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14) | 14,50-71,113-148 | Time filtering and newest-window selection compare timestamp strings, which breaks with timezone offsets or mixed ISO representations. |
| medium | [cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:121) | 121-180 | Report commands call the initializing DB connector, so a typo in `--db` silently creates an empty database and reports no jobs. |
| low | [db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) | 13-27,52-59 | There is no schema versioning or migration path; existing incompatible databases are silently accepted until later failures. |
| low | [parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:153) | 153-156 | Empty `User` and `Partition` values are accepted, creating blank report groups instead of rejecting malformed rows. |
| low | [tests/test_ingest.py](/work/tests/test_ingest.py:40) | 40-64 | Tests cover rank downgrades but miss equal-rank stale overwrites and changed-resource reingests, the highest-risk ingest cases. |

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **about 150 LOC**, including upsert freshness/equality logic, parser validation, report DB open semantics, timestamp normalization policy, and regression tests.

issues.description: Older same-rank lifecycle records can overwrite fresher terminal records because updates do not compare reference timestamps.
Re-ingest treats rows as unchanged when only state/end/elapsed match, ignoring changed user, partition, CPU, GPU, submit/start, and exit code fields.
Unknown Slurm states default to terminal rank, so active states like CONFIGURING can block later valid RUNNING updates.
Negative GPU or CPU counts are accepted and can produce negative usage-hour reports.
Time filtering and newest-window selection compare timestamp strings, which breaks with timezone offsets or mixed ISO representations.
Report commands call the initializing DB connector, so a typo in --db silently creates an empty database and reports no jobs.
There is no schema versioning or migration path; existing incompatible databases are silently accepted until later failures.
Empty User and Partition values are accepted, creating blank report groups instead of rejecting malformed rows.
Tests cover rank downgrades but miss equal-rank stale overwrites and changed-resource reingests, the highest-risk ingest cases.
